l: Developer tools for the 75% who build their own.

The ISVs want to sell you a platform. We want to give you libraries.

p: The European power market data landscape is fragmented. Every exchange has its own API, its own data format, its own quirks. The community alternatives (entsoe-py, kipe/nordpool) are volunteer-maintained and frequently break when APIs change.
nexa-marketdata provides a single, well-tested client that handles:
Multiple exchanges through a consistent interface
15-minute MTU data natively (not bolted on as an afterthought)
Rate limiting so you do not get throttled at 03:00
Caching to avoid redundant API calls on repeated historical requests
Type-safe models with strict mypy compliance and Pydantic v2

p: Building bids for European power auctions is complex. EUPHEMIA supports block bids, linked orders, exclusive groups, and merit-order curves, each with specific constraints that vary by exchange. Getting the domain model wrong means rejected bids or unintended market exposure.
Type-safe bid construction via Pydantic v2 models with strict validation
DataFrame-first API for building merit-order curves from pandas DataFrames
15-minute MTU support natively across all bid types (hourly and quarter-hourly)
EUPHEMIA-compatible output including block, linked, indivisible, and exclusive bids
Nord Pool serialisation converting order books to Nord Pool Auction API payloads
Pre-submission validation catching EUPHEMIA violations, data quality issues, and temporal constraints

l: Build a merit-order curve from a DataFrame

c:
import pandas as pd
from decimal import Decimal
from datetime import datetime
from zoneinfo import ZoneInfo
from nexa_bidkit import (
    CurveType,
    MTUDuration,
    MTUInterval,
    from_dataframe,
)

# Your bid data as a DataFrame
df = pd.DataFrame({
    "price": [10.5, 25.0, 45.0, 80.0],
    "volume": [50, 100, 75, 25],
})

# Define the MTU this curve applies to
mtu = MTUInterval.from_start(
    datetime(2026, 4, 1, 13, 0, tzinfo=ZoneInfo("Europe/Oslo")),
    MTUDuration.QUARTER_HOURLY,
)

# Convert to a validated supply curve
curve = from_dataframe(df, curve_type=CurveType.SUPPLY, mtu=mtu)

print(f"Total volume: {curve.total_volume} MW")
print(f"Price range: {curve.min_price} - {curve.max_price} EUR/MWh")

from decimal import Decimal
from datetime import datetime
from zoneinfo import ZoneInfo
from nexa_bidkit import (
    BiddingZone,
    Direction,
    DeliveryPeriod,
    MTUDuration,
    block_bid,
    indivisible_block_bid,
    linked_block_bid,
    exclusive_group,
)

delivery = DeliveryPeriod(
    start=datetime(2026, 4, 1, 10, 0, tzinfo=ZoneInfo("Europe/Oslo")),
    end=datetime(2026, 4, 1, 14, 0, tzinfo=ZoneInfo("Europe/Oslo")),
    duration=MTUDuration.QUARTER_HOURLY,
)

# Partially fillable block bid (50%+ fill accepted)
peak_bid = block_bid(
    bidding_zone=BiddingZone.NO1,
    direction=Direction.SELL,
    delivery_period=delivery,
    price=Decimal("55.0"),
    volume=Decimal("100"),
    min_acceptance_ratio=Decimal("0.5"),
)

# Must-run: all-or-nothing
must_run = indivisible_block_bid(
    bidding_zone=BiddingZone.NO1,
    direction=Direction.SELL,
    delivery_period=delivery,
    price=Decimal("25.0"),
    volume=Decimal("50"),
)

# Linked bid: only accepted if must_run is accepted
ramp_up = linked_block_bid(
    parent_bid_id=must_run.bid_id,
    bidding_zone=BiddingZone.NO1,
    direction=Direction.SELL,
    delivery_period=delivery,
    price=Decimal("35.0"),
    volume=Decimal("25"),
)

# Validate before gate closure

# Export to pandas for review

from nexa_bidkit.nordpool import order_book_to_nord_pool

# Map (MTUInterval, BiddingZone) to Nord Pool contract IDs
# Populate this from Nord Pool's products API at runtime
def resolve_contract(mtu, zone):

submission = order_book_to_nord_pool(
    book,
    auction_id="DA-2026-04-01",
    portfolio="my-portfolio",
    contract_id_resolver=resolve_contract,
)

print(f"Curve orders:        {len(submission.curve_orders)}")
print(f"Block orders:        {len(submission.block_orders)}")
print(f"Linked block orders: {len(submission.linked_block_orders)}")

The API, documentation, and feature set are under active development and subject to change. Bid building, validation, and XML serialisation are stable. TSO response parsing and Pandas integration are planned.

pip install nexa-mfrr-nordic-eam[pandas]

p: The Nordic mFRR energy activation market (EAM) went live on 4 March 2025 as part of the Nordic Balancing Model (NBM). It operates on 15-minute Market Time Units (MTUs). Balancing Service Providers (BSPs) submit bids via CIM XML documents over ECP/EDX to their connecting TSO.
This library handles the full BSP workflow for bid submission:
Simple bids — divisible and indivisible, with full attribute support (volume, price, resource, product type, duration constraints)
Complex bid groups — ExclusiveGroup, MultipartGroup, and InclusiveGroup with group-level validation
Technically linked bids — TechnicalLink builder groups bids across MTUs under a shared link ID to prevent double-activation
Conditionally linked bids — adjust bid availability in QH0 based on activation outcomes in QH-1 or QH-2
TSO configurations — Statnett (NO), Svenska kraftnat (SE), and Energinet (DK) fully configured
MARI/pre-MARI mode — toggle affects price limits, timing calculations, and validation rules
CIM XML serialisation — generates compliant ReserveBid_MarketDocument XML per the NBM ReserveBid schema
Timing helpers — gate closure calculations, MTU boundaries, DST handling
What it does not do: manage your ECP/EDX endpoint. That is infrastructure you deploy and operate separately. This library generates the XML documents you send through your endpoint.

l: Submit a simple divisible bid to Statnett

c:
from datetime import datetime, timezone
from nexa_mfrr_eam import (
    Bid, BidDocument, Direction, MarketProductType,
    BiddingZone, TSO, MARIMode,
)

# Create a simple divisible up-regulation bid
bid = (
    Bid.up(volume_mw=50, price_eur=85.50)
    .divisible(min_volume_mw=10)
    .for_mtu("2026-03-21T10:00Z")
    .resource("NOKG90901", coding_scheme="NNO")  # Statnett regulation object
    .product_type(MarketProductType.SCHEDULED_AND_DIRECT)  # A07
    .build()
)

# Wrap in a document targeting Statnett
doc = (
    BidDocument(tso=TSO.STATNETT)
    .sender(party_id="9999909919920", coding_scheme="A10")  # GS1
    .add_bid(bid)
    .build()
)

# Validate against Statnett-specific rules (pre-MARI timing)
errors = doc.validate(mari_mode=MARIMode.PRE_MARI)
if errors:
    for e in errors:
        print(f"  {e}")
else:
    xml_bytes = doc.to_xml()
    # Send xml_bytes via your ECP endpoint to Statnett

p: Technical linking ensures a resource is not double-activated when a bid in one MTU is activated via direct activation and is still ramping during the next MTU.

c:
from nexa_mfrr_eam import TechnicalLink, Direction, MarketProductType

link = (
    TechnicalLink(bidding_zone=BiddingZone.SE3)
    .resource("REG-OBJ-SE-001", coding_scheme="A01")  # EIC
    .add_mtu(
        mtu="2026-03-21T10:00Z",
        direction=Direction.UP,
        volume_mw=25,
        price_eur=90.00,
        product_type=MarketProductType.SCHEDULED_AND_DIRECT,
    )
    .add_mtu(
        mtu="2026-03-21T10:15Z",
        direction=Direction.UP,
        volume_mw=25,
        price_eur=90.00,
        product_type=MarketProductType.SCHEDULED_AND_DIRECT,
    )
    .build()
)

from nexa_mfrr_eam import ExclusiveGroup, MarketProductType

group = (

    .for_mtu("2026-03-21T10:00Z")
    .add_bid(
        Bid.up(volume_mw=30, price_eur=60.00)
        .indivisible()
        .resource("NOKG90901", coding_scheme="NNO")
    )
    .add_bid(
        Bid.up(volume_mw=50, price_eur=80.00)
        .divisible(min_volume_mw=10)
        .resource("NOKG90902", coding_scheme="NNO")
    )
    .product_type(MarketProductType.SCHEDULED_ONLY)
    .build()
)

p: Adjust bid availability in QH0 based on activation outcomes in QH-1.

c:
from nexa_mfrr_eam import ConditionalStatus

bid_qh_minus_1 = (
    Bid.up(volume_mw=30, price_eur=70.00)
    .divisible(min_volume_mw=5)
    .for_mtu("2026-03-21T10:15Z")
    .resource("NOKG90901", coding_scheme="NNO")
    .build()
)

# Bid is conditionally available in 10:30
# only if the linked bid in 10:15 was NOT activated
bid_qh_0 = (
    Bid.up(volume_mw=30, price_eur=70.00)
    .divisible(min_volume_mw=5)
    .for_mtu("2026-03-21T10:30Z")
    .resource("NOKG90901", coding_scheme="NNO")
    .conditionally_available()  # A65
    .link_to(bid_qh_minus_1, status=ConditionalStatus.NOT_AVAILABLE_IF_ACTIVATED)  # A55
    .build()
)

p: The mFRR EAM operates on 15-minute MTUs. There are 96 MTUs per day. Transition days during daylight saving time changes have 92 or 100 MTUs. The library handles DST correctly throughout.

p: The library generates ReserveBid_MarketDocument XML compliant with the NBM ReserveBid schema (XSD version 7.2). Element ordering follows the XSD xs:sequence strictly.
Statnett: minimum bid 10 MW; heartbeat required; supports period shift and faster activation bids
Svenska kraftnat: 6-minute document cut-off; heartbeat every 5 minutes
Energinet: no heartbeat; mktPSRType.psrType mandatory; local direct activation model
Fingrid: planned; max 2000 bids per message; supports inclusive bids for aggregated resources

Exchange coverage: Adding support for a new exchange or data source? Open an issue first so we can discuss the approach.
